```{r setup}
library(chromatographR)
```

##### 1. How should I format my data for analysis in `chromatographR`?

`chromatographR` functions expect chromatograms to be in wide format with retention times as rownames. Thus, if you have a csv file with retention times in the first column, you should be able to read the files into R as follows:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
lapply(vector_of_file_paths, function(f){
  read.csv(f, row.names = 1)
})
```

If you have chromatograms in "long" format, you will need to reshape them into wide format before proceeding with the analysis.

\n

##### 2. Some of my peaks aren't being integrated when I run `get_peaks`.

`get_peaks` keeps every peak it fits, but `filter_peaks` with `max_fwhm` discards peaks wider than that, so your widest peaks are the first to go. What counts as a sensible value depends on your data, so measure your peak widths first (see the [peak-finding article](https://ethanbass.github.io/chromatographR/articles/peak-finding.html)). In the example below, `max_fwhm = 0.12` drops many of the wider peaks that `get_peaks` found. If peaks are still missing, try adjusting `smooth_window`, which is passed to `find_peaks`.

```{r}
data(Sa_warp)
par(mfrow=c(2,1))
pks <- get_peaks(Sa_warp, lambdas = "210", fit = "egh")
plot(pks, main = "All peaks")
plot(filter_peaks(pks, max_fwhm = 0.12), main = "`max_fwhm` = 0.12")
```
